tenders.title: S30135 Impulse Geophysics Surveys
tenders.summary: This additional work order is required to deliver an updated, network wide survey of ageing concrete road surfaces across the Strategic Road Network, many of which are now reaching the end of their de
tenders.detailedDescription: This additional work order is required to deliver an updated, network wide survey of ageing concrete road surfaces across the Strategic Road Network, many of which are now reaching the end of their design life and present increasing risk if not properly understood and managed. The current data used to plan maintenance and renewals is outdated due to network changes and previous works, meaning decisions could otherwise be made on incomplete or inaccurate information. This commission will provide a consistent, up to date picture of road condition using proven survey methods (including radar and visual inspections), enabling informed, evidence based decisions on where repairs or full reconstruction are most urgently needed, helping to prevent asset failure and minimise safety risks to road users. It is also critical that this is delivered as a single coordinated programme using the same methodology as previous surveys to ensure data consistency and avoid inefficiencies, delays, and fragmented information that would weaken strategic planning and increase long term costs. Timely delivery (targeting completion of surveys by October 2026) is essential to support upcoming investment and maintenance programmes and maintain safe, reliable operation of the network.

tenders.summary: This work order will enable National Highways to bring in specialist technical support to deliver the Growth and Housing Accelerator Fund, a £165 million programme designed to unlock stalled housing a
tenders.detailedDescription: This work order will enable National Highways to bring in specialist technical support to deliver the Growth and Housing Accelerator Fund, a £165 million programme designed to unlock stalled housing and employment developments that are currently delayed due to funding gaps and the need to ensure the strategic road network remains safe and fit for purpose. Without this support, there is a risk that essential infrastructure upgrades (such as junction improvements or new links) are not properly planned or delivered in time, which could lead to increased traffic pressures, safety concerns, and continued delays to much needed homes and jobs. The work involves assessing and prioritising schemes, building strong business cases, managing risks, and overseeing delivery to ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget through to 2031. Given the scale of investment, the government's housing targets, and the safety implications of unmanaged traffic growth, appointing this capability is both urgent and essential to ensure the programme delivers value and prevents wider operational and safety issues across the network.

tenders.title: S30129 Road Design DMRB Standards Research & Development CD127, CD109 & CD116
tenders.summary: National Highways is commissioning a programme of research to review and potentially modernise key road design standards, with a strong focus on safety, efficiency and future capacity of the strategic
tenders.detailedDescription: National Highways is commissioning a programme of research to review and potentially modernise key road design standards, with a strong focus on safety, efficiency and future capacity of the strategic road network. This work will examine whether motorways and major roads could safely carry more lanes than currently allowed, and whether alternative road layouts (such as 2+1 or 2+2 configurations with central barriers) could deliver similar performance at lower cost, while maintaining or improving safety. It will also assess whether current design rules around speed and visibility (including how we set design speeds for rural roads and how small objects must be detectable by drivers) are still appropriate, as these have direct implications for collision risk and compliance. Finally, it will review the design of large, complex junctions (such as major roundabouts) to ensure current standards do not contain gaps that could lead to operational issues or safety concerns. This work is important and time-sensitive because existing standards may be limiting capacity, increasing costs, or unintentionally introducing safety risks, and updating them could enable more efficient, safer and more deliverable schemes across the network.
